cells.tense: What you see is landing plainly in the meaning you share with other people, and there is still room to feed it.
cells.act: put the frame on the table before anyone asks
cells.ask: When a group gathers around something shared — a meal, a meeting — say once, plainly, what it is for, before anyone asks why you are there. Then leave it standing.
cells.core:
When enough people are carrying the same story, you can still see it whole and say what it's for. Many versions sit easily beside each other in you, and the room gets steadier company for it. You say the frame early, before anyone asks, and it lands as clear rather than loud.

This balance feeds what comes next. Put that frame on the table once, plainly, the next time people gather around something shared — say what it is for, then leave it alone. Some may say the group took it from you. The words were yours, and saying them aloud carried what you'd seen its last step — noticing is one thing, and naming it to the room is another.
cells.sheetLine: You hold many truths at once and they stay usable.
cells.verb: holding many truths at once and letting them land
cells.place: in shared meaning and the things a community keeps passing down

cells.tense: You will be bracing against the new claim and the new group before either one has had a chance to arrive.
cells.act: turn toward the one direction and stop surveying
cells.ask: Choose one practice forming in a shared room — a ritual, a way of doing it — and stand inside it. Don't rank it against others and don't announce it. One heading for a few days.
cells.core:
Where many ways of doing things have built up, you're gathering the next possibility before you've finished carrying the last. Every new claim gets advanced, every new group gets explained, and the weight doesn't leave you tired so much as pre-committed. You're promising the future what the present hasn't finished.

Answer the many truths with one direction. Take the shared thing already forming — the ritual, the way a group does it — and stand inside it a few days. No ranking, no announcement. When you're sitting like a finished thing instead of reaching for the next one, the shine comes from the thing you built, not from you.
cells.sheetLine: You know the next arrival before it's shown up.

cells.tense: You went along with the shared way of things a while back, and you have watched from beside it since.
cells.act: meet someone in the middle and go on together
cells.ask: Take one person and one practice — a weekly walk, a meal, the same song. Do it with them, in the middle, and keep going past the first time. Twice makes it shared.
cells.core:
In the shared things you move through — the meal, the meeting, the words other people use — what you see has gone quiet. You take it all in and give back very little, and from the outside that looks like you dropped out of the room. You stepped beside it a while back, and this is what beside looks like.

Join one current instead of watching it pass. Take one practice you already half-share with someone — the weekly walk, the meal, the words you both grew up using — and do it with them, in the middle, not from a distance. Then do it again past the first time. Two times is where a thing stops being yours alone.
cells.sheetLine: You hear everything and hand back very little.

cells.tense: You are keeping the meaning of a group straight, right now, while telling the story that you just go along with it.
cells.act: do the fair thing where no one will see
cells.ask: The next small unfairness in a shared room — a word left out, a weight handed to the same person again — fix it quietly. No announcement, no credit. Doing it unseen is enough.
cells.core:
Shared meaning holds longer around you because you quietly keep it honest — you know which version of the story is true, you know which rule the room pretends not to have, and you adjust for it without saying so. Your story is that you go along with other people's way of things. The record on you is longer than that.

So do the fair thing where nobody sees. The next small unfairness in the shared room — a word left out of the account, a weight given to the same person again — fix it quietly, before anyone asks, and keep no record of it. Letting it stay unsaid is how the room stays clean, and how the one doing the cleaning stays unseen.
cells.sheetLine: You keep the shared thing honest and call yourself a guest.
cells.verb: holding many truths at once and letting them land
